title: wt sync owner --json
description: What `wt sync owner --json` prints on stdout: one object, for an answer or a refusal. A refusal has the reason in refusal and exits non-zero; every answer, whatever into says, exits 0; a command line wt cannot read prints no object and exits non-zero. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

work.description: The worktree as it was named; null for the one the command ran in.

branch.description: The branch whose line was read; null when the line was not read.

tip.description: The line's tip, whose version of the file the lines are of; null when the line was not read.

path.description: The file, from the worktree's root; null when it was not resolved.

lines.description: The lines answered for, the whole file when none were given; null when they were not resolved.

edited.description: Whether the worktree has uncommitted changes, staged or not, in or right beside those lines. The answer is for the committed lines either way.

owners.description: The commits of the line that last changed some of the lines, newest first.

foldsInto.description: For an owner that is a fixup!, squash! or amend! commit, the commit a fold makes it part of; null otherwise, and when its subject names no one commit.

lines.description: The lines it owns, in order.

unowned.description: The lines no commit of the line changed: the line's base already has them.

verdict.description: What a fold of the line in place makes of a change to exactly those lines, committed as a fixup of this commit: folds, when it applies there and the rest of the line replays clean; does-not-fold, when a later commit has its context; cannot-tell; refused, when the run would not make the fold.

needs.description: For does-not-fold, the later commit that carries the context; null otherwise.

why.description: For cannot-tell and refused, the reason; null otherwise.

into.description: The commit --into names, and the verdict; null without --into, and for a refusal.

refusal.description: Why there is no answer, in the words printed on stderr; null when there is one.

layer.description: The layer branch the commit is in; the line's own branch above the top layer.

span.description: Lines from to to, inclusive, of the file as the line's tip has it.
